transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. I'm a high school teacher, and I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble lately with... well, with keeping my focus on certain things. It's probably normal, you know, everyone gets distracted, right? But I'll sit down with a stack of student essays or a new curriculum document, and I'll fully intend to get through them. And then, maybe ten minutes later, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page. My mind just sort of wanders off to three other things, and I haven't really taken in a single word. I feel terrible about it because I really do care about my students and my job. Is that... is that the kind of thing you help people with?
When your mind wanders while you're trying to focus, what kinds of thoughts are pulling your attention away—are they specific worries or fears, or more just random unrelated thoughts?

Oh, no, it's definitely not worries or fears. I don't want you to think I'm, like, overly anxious or stressed out, because I'm really not! I have a great life. It's more just... well, completely random things, I guess? 

Like, I'll be looking at a student's thesis statement, and suddenly I'm wondering if I remembered to buy coffee filters, or I'm thinking about a documentary I watched three days ago, or just... I don't know, what I'm going to make for dinner. Just silly, harmless stuff, really. I haven't kept a super close track of it, but it's never anything bad or upsetting. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... is it normal for it to just be random noise like that?
Thinking back, did you have similar trouble focusing or staying on task as a child or teenager, or is this something that's new for you recently?

Well, I guess... um, I guess it isn't entirely new. But I really don't want to sound like I was a bad student or a troublemaker, because I promise I wasn't! I always wanted to do well and please my teachers. 

It's just that, even way back in primary school, my report cards would usually say things like... well, they would say I was bright, which was very nice of them, but then they would add that I was careless, or that I would not finish my work unless I was being closely supervised. And my parents were always finding these crumpled worksheets shoved at the very bottom of my backpack that I had just completely forgotten to turn in. 

I feel so embarrassed even admitting that to you now, especially since I am a teacher myself. I was just a little scattered back then, I suppose? A lot of kids are a bit disorganized like that, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound incredibly irresponsible... did I answer your question okay?

Do you notice this same difficulty focusing and staying on task happening in other parts of your life outside of grading and lesson planning—like at home with chores, paperwork, or conversations—or is it mostly limited to your work tasks?

Well... I suppose it's not just the lesson planning. I try really hard to keep on top of things at home, I really do, but... honestly, my wife has actually started taking over paying the bills and keeping track of all our household reminders. I feel awful making her do that, but she just couldn't really count on me to remember them, and I didn't want to cause any late fees or anything. She's so great and patient about it, really. 

And, um... at work... I'm a little ashamed to say this, because I really do love my job and respect my school, but my missed follow-through with some of the administrative stuff got to the point where... well, my department chair actually put me on a support plan. They were incredibly nice about it! It's just to help me, it's not a punishment or anything like that, I promise. But I guess it means it has become a bit of a serious issue lately. 

Does that... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information. I really don't want to sound like a terrible husband or a bad employee, I just... I've been struggling to keep all the plates spinning, I guess.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

Oh, no, no, not at all! I really don't want you to think I'm hyperactive or bouncing off the walls or anything. I'm actually a pretty calm person, I think! I don't really get restless or fidgety... I mean, I sit still during all my staff meetings and everything. And I definitely don't try to interrupt people. I always try to be polite and listen when others are talking. 

I really try to think things through, too. I don't want to cause any problems or be disruptive, you know? So, no, I wouldn't say I have any of those issues. I hope that's okay? Like, it's alright that I just have the focus problems and not the... the hyper kind of stuff? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.

Over the past several months, have you noticed any changes in your mood, energy, or sleep—like feeling persistently down, unusually tired, or having trouble sleeping—that might be affecting your concentration?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. My mood has been completely fine, really! I mean, I'm generally a pretty happy person, I think. I definitely don't feel persistently down or anything like that. I'd hate for you to think I was hiding something like depression from you, but I promise my mood is okay. 

And my sleep is... well, it's pretty normal. I try really hard to get a good night's rest so I can be, you know, present and upbeat for my students. So I haven't noticed any unusual tiredness. Just the normal amount of tired you get from teaching teenagers all day! 

Does that make sense? I hope it's not a problem that I don't have those other symptoms. Like, it's okay if it's just the concentration stuff on its own, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate answers I can so I'm not wasting your time.

Would you say these concentration difficulties have been present fairly continuously since childhood through adulthood, or were there stretches of time—like certain years—where you didn't have much trouble focusing at all?

Well... I mean, I guess it's always been there, to some degree. I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I was actually a really happy kid, and I liked school. But, um... yeah, if I look back, it hasn't really stopped at any point. 

Even back in primary school, my parents used to find these crumpled-up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I had just... completely forgotten to turn in. I always felt so bad when they found them. And my report cards, they usually said things like... well, they'd say I was "bright but careless," or that I didn't finish my work unless the teacher was right there supervising me. 

They weren't being mean, the teachers, I know they were just trying to help me do my best. But I guess I've just always struggled with keeping track of things and staying on task, even back then. I hope that's the kind of background information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
